usage.goal: Count objects from 1 to 15 and say how many things you see or have.
usage.canDoStatement: I can count simple objects and say how many there are.

scenes.scenario: I have one book, two pens, and three pencils.

check.question: How many pencils do I have?

scenes.imageBrief: Bright desk scene with exactly 1 book, 2 pens, and 3 pencils, clearly visible and easy to count.

scenes.imageBrief: Clean fruit display showing 7 apples, 8 oranges, and 9 bananas in grouped rows.

reading.text: This is my classroom. I have one teacher and two friends near me. There are three windows and four tables. I see five bags and six books. There are seven pictures on the wall. Our class has fifteen students.

video.title: Count With Me
video.idea: 30–45 second video. A learner looks around a room and counts objects aloud, then pauses to let the viewer answer before revealing the number.
video.scriptStarter: I see one clock. There are two windows. I see three plants. How many chairs can you see?

usage.goal: Understand and say larger numbers for age, quantity, and simple real-life facts.

usage.goal: Recognize simple maths symbols and use a few common maths words in easy expressions.
usage.canDoStatement: I can understand a few basic maths words and symbols.

scenes.scenario: Two plus one is three. Four minus one is three. Two times two is four.

check.question: What does four minus one equal?

scenes.imageBrief: Three simple math symbol cards for plus, minus, and times, each with one easy example.

scenes.scenario: Six divided by two is three. Fifty percent means half.
scenes.imageBrief: Two-card set: one shows 6 ÷ 2 = 3, the other shows a circle half-filled to explain 50 percent.

reading.title: Math Class
reading.text: In math class, we use plus and minus every day. Today, the teacher writes six divided by two on the board. Then she shows fifty percent on a circle chart. The class says the answers together.
reading.imageBrief: Simple classroom math lesson with a board and a percentage pie chart.
